title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page sets up isomorphisms (40)-(44). Here U_{0,3} = P^1 minus {0,1,∞} = M_{0,4}. S_3 = D_3 acts on it by the anharmonic group. τ is complex conjugation, which commutes with S_3. π_{0,3}^{D_3} and π_{0,3}^{D_3,τ} are the equivariant (orbifold) fundamental groups of U_{0,3} for the actions of S_3 and of S_3×{1,τ}. The quotient λ-line/S_3 is the j-line, an orbifold with cone points of order 2 and 3 and one cusp. Its orbifold fundamental group is the triangle group (2,3,∞) = PSL(2,Z). With τ added, one gets the extended modular group PGL(2,Z) = GL(2,Z)/±1, acting on the upper half-plane by homographies and anti-homographies. This gives (44) PSL(2,Z) ≅ π_{0,3}^{D_3} ≅ π_{0,3}/⟨ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^3⟩ and (43) PGL(2,Z) ≅ π_{0,3}^{D_3,τ}.

This page draws three consequences.
(i) The distinguished elements ρ, σ_i, τ_i, σ̃_i, ε_i, ℓ_i of Π_{0,3}^{D_3,τ} can be read as explicit elements of GL(2,Z)/±1. Lifting them further to GL(2,Z) gives a 'most pleasant formulation', which G. says he developed and used extensively in his notes of 'last year (1981)'. This dates the page to 1982.
(ii) Proposed generalization to Π_{0,n} 'and variants', associated with regular n-gons. The natural reading is the sphere minus the n-th roots of unity with its dihedral D_n symmetry, plus complex conjugation. The quotient orbifold is P^1 with a cone point of order n (0 and ∞ identified), a cone point of order 2 (at w = z^n = -1) and a cusp (w = 1). So the equivariant π_1 is the triangle group (2,n,∞), i.e. the Hecke group H_n ⊂ PSL(2,R), generated by z ↦ -1/z and z ↦ z + 2cos(π/n). Its extended version lies in PGL(2,R). These are the 'remarkable discrete subgroups' of GL(2,R) he alludes to. For n = 3 one recovers PSL(2,Z) and PGL(2,Z).
(iii) Section 5, the cartographic interpretation of (40). An equivalence of isotopy categories, in both the oriented and non-oriented theories:
- on one side, 'triangular' maps X, whose faces have order dividing 3 (monogons or triangles), corresponding to PSL(2,Z)-sets;
- on the other side, weighted triangular maps X' (vertices labelled 0,1,∞, i.e. dessins/hypermaps, corresponding to Γ(2) ≅ free group F_2) equipped with an S_3-action permuting the weights.
The next page makes it explicit:
- From X' to X: take X = X'/S_3, ramified of index 3 at face centres, index 2 at edge midpoints, and at the weighted vertices.
- From X to X': take the barycentric subdivision of X, view its triangles as flags, and build a principal S_3 ramified cover from the flag-adjacency operators τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞.
This is the combinatorial form of the Galois correspondence for Γ(2) ⊲ PSL(2,Z) with quotient S_3. Equivalently: PSL(2,Z)-sets are the same as Γ(2)-sets with compatible S_3-equivariance, via induction/descent.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The isomorphisms are correct: (2,3,∞) = PSL(2,Z), and its extension by an orientation-reversing involution is PGL(2,Z). The generalization to n-gons is only sketched and not proved, and the meaning of 'Π_{0,n} et variantes' is left implicit.
The description 'faces of order dividing three' is correct for PSL(2,Z)-sets viewed as maps: triangles plus monogons from the order-3 fixed points.

ideas.what: PSL(2,Z) and PGL(2,Z) as equivariant fundamental groups of P^1-{0,1,∞} under the anharmonic S_3 (and S_3×complex conjugation)
ideas.modern_name: orbifold fundamental group of the j-line / modular orbifold; triangle group (2,3,∞)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein, Fricke); dessins viewpoint: Grothendieck, Esquisse (1984); Jones-Singerman
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of cartographic groups and the modular group

ideas.what: Distinguished elements of the equivariant π_1 (ρ, σ_i, τ_i, ε_i, ℓ_i) realised as explicit matrices in GL(2,Z), lifting beyond ±1
ideas.modern_name: explicit matrix model of the extended modular group / cartographic group C_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in the theory of maps (Jones-Singerman 1978); Grothendieck's own 1981 notes

ideas.what: Generalization to the sphere minus n points with D_n symmetry: groups realised as discrete subgroups of GL(2,R)
ideas.modern_name: Hecke groups H_n = triangle groups (2,n,∞) and extended Hecke groups; n-gonal maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hecke (1936); maps and Hecke groups: Singerman, Jones-Singerman (1970s)

ideas.what: Equivalence between triangular maps (faces of order 1 or 3) and weighted triangulations (dessins) with an S_3-action permuting the weights, via quotient and barycentric subdivision / principal S_3 cover
ideas.modern_name: Galois descent for Γ(2) ⊲ PSL(2,Z), quotient S_3; dessins vs. trivalent/triangular maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones-Singerman, Grothendieck (Esquisse), Malle-Matzat, Schneps et al.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses triangulations and finite-index subgroups of the modular group, but not this S_3-equivariant equivalence explicitly (unsure)

missed.claim: Historical datum: G. states that the lifted GL(2,Z) formulation of the cartographic and Teichmüller elements was 'developed and used extensively' in his 1981 notes. This dates the matrix approach and this page (1982).
missed.quote: donnant lieu à une formulation des plus sympathiques, que j'ai développée et utilisée extensivement dans mes notes de l'an dernier (1981)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Locates where in the archive his explicit modular-group computations for dessins live. Useful for historians tracing the pre-Esquisse genesis of dessins d'enfants.

deep.surprise_reason: Every mathematical point is classical or a standard part of dessins theory: (2,3,∞) = PSL(2,Z), its extension PGL(2,Z), Hecke groups for n-gons, and Galois descent from Γ(2) to PSL(2,Z). The only interest is historical: the dating and the explicit S_3-equivariant formulation in Grothendieck's own framework.
transcription_corrections: Line before 'comme sous-groupes discrets': the first group should read 'Sl(2,Z)/±1 resp. Gl(2,Z)/±1', matching (44)/(43), not 'Gl ... resp. Gl'.
'que les cas[?] en considérant[?] ensuite[?] à faire correspondre' is uncertain. The sense is that one can further lift each element to GL(2,Z); the exact words cannot be read with confidence.
'Π_{0,n} {+et variantes+}' and the inserted 'n' before 'polygones réguliers' are correct as insertions; 'cf. au voisinage précédemment' is doubtful.
'Dans l'interprétation "cartographique"' and 'dont toutes les faces sont d'ordre divisant trois, i.e. sont des monogones ou des triangles' are confirmed by the image.
